decision: tad is released by release-please (versions and changelog from conventional commits) with the package conveyor building binaries in the same run; the tag-triggered workflow is gone.
why: One release path, no manual version bumps; a tag made with GitHub's own token cannot start another workflow, so the binaries are built in the same run.
rejected: Tagging by hand with land --tag as the release path; keeping both paths.

decision: The lab machine moves each repository's tad pin (bin/update-pins.sh, weekly), landing through land so each repository's CI decides.
why: A pull request opened by a workflow with GitHub's own token starts no CI, so a pure-GitHub updater would open unchecked pull requests; the lab machine already holds a token and lands through checks.
rejected: A GitHub workflow with GitHub's token (its pull requests start no CI); the author's personal token as a secret in four repositories (spreads the key); a GitHub App (the clean CI-native way - needs the author's setup; a later upgrade).

decision: tad in Rust: tables declared as data (after Frictionless Table Schema); one tool - check, canonical form, row edits with a check, documents rendered from data; proven equal to the Python version on all four repositories (same verdicts, same documents) before any switch; delivered by the package conveyor instead of vendored; ocoeco's shapes become a tad declaration. The tool is delivered by the package conveyor (for CI and machines); the library is taken as a Rhizoid cutting where a project builds on it (ocoeco) - as tad's own path already says, a rhizcut in every repository. Corrected 2026-11-12 by 2026-11-12-sql-again: SQL is not optional - tad answers real SQL through an embedded SQLite.
why: The author: tad stays general and Python leaves. The four schemas need no database engine: their 41 tables use only patterns, allowed values, required fields and one list column.
rejected: Rust bindings to DuckDB keeping schema.sql (a database engine to validate text); Dolt (a separate store); keeping the vendored copies.

decision: When the four repositories switch to tad, their documents are re-rendered by today's renderer; the canon's and Rhizoid's change visibly, and that is said in the switch's own change.
why: Their vendored copies are older; the switch is the first time they get today's renderer. A change people did not expect should be announced, not discovered.
rejected: Porting the older renderers too, to switch without visible change.

decision: tad answers real SQL again: tad sql runs a statement over the declared tables through an embedded SQLite - a query reads them, a change is checked by tad (every row and rule) before the tables are written back in canonical form, as the Python version did with DuckDB. Proven equal on the four repositories' own queries before anyone relies on it.
why: The author, 2026-11-12: the whole point of tad is that it can be used with real SQL; and lab-agent's journal will be tad tables that must be queried. The Rust rewrite had dropped SQL as optional - that was wrong.
rejected: No SQL (the rewrite's choice - it left tad unable to answer questions about its own data); GlueSQL (pure Rust, storage as a trait, but younger and a smaller dialect); DataFusion (built for analytics at scale, heavy for this); DuckDB again (a large engine to embed, and the declaration already gives the types).
